3º de Primaria · Inglés

Writing about myself

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

Tienes un amigo por correspondencia en Inglaterra y quieres presentarte por escrito. ¿Qué cosas le contarías de ti y cómo lo ordenarías?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

Primero haces un plan: nombre y edad, dónde vives, tu familia, lo que te gusta y lo que sabes hacer. Después escribes frases cortas con I'm, I've got, I like y I can, unidas con and, but y because. ¡Y al final lo repasas!

2

Aprende15 apartados

Para empezar: A letter from Jamie

Dear Paula,

Hi! My name is Jamie and I'm your new pen pal. I'm nine years old and I live in Edinburgh, in Scotland. It's a beautiful city with an old castle on a hill.

I've got short red hair and green eyes, and I wear glasses. I'm quite tall. My friends say I'm funny and friendly, but I'm a bit shy with new people.

I live with my mum, my dad and my little brother, Callum. He's five and he's very noisy! We've got a dog called Haggis. He's black and white and he loves running on the beach.

I love reading adventure stories and playing the bagpipes. Do you know them? They're a Scottish instrument. I don't like football, but I like swimming. My favourite food is fish and chips.

When I grow up, I want to be a vet because I love animals.

What about you? What do you like doing? Have you got any pets? Please write soon!

Best wishes,
Jamie

1. All about me

Writing about yourself is a great way to use all the English you know. In a text about you, you can write: your name and age, where you live, what you look like, your family and pets, what you like and what you can do.

You already know the sentences! «I'm Carla.» «I'm eight.» «I've got a brother.» «I like pizza.» «I can swim.» Ahora solo hay que ordenarlas y unirlas para que formen un texto bonito.

2. Looks and personality

When we write about ourselves, we can describe two things: our looks (aspecto físico) and our personality (forma de ser).

Looks: we use I've got for hair and eyes, and I'm for height.

  • «I've got long / short / curly (rizado) / straight (liso) brown hair.»
  • «I've got blue / green / brown eyes.»
  • «I'm tall / short / medium height.» «I wear glasses.» (llevo gafas)

Look at the order: size + type + colour + hair: «long curly black hair».

Personality: we use I'm.

  • friendly (simpático), kind (amable), funny (gracioso), shy (tímido), clever (listo), brave (valiente), chatty (hablador), calm (tranquilo), hard-working (trabajador).

We can make them softer or stronger: «I'm a bit shy.» (un poco) «I'm very chatty!»

Activity: write two sentences about your looks and two about your personality.

3. Plan first: a mind map

Before writing, make a mind map (mapa de ideas). Write ME in the centre. Draw lines to five bubbles: name and age, home, family, likes and abilities. In each bubble, write words, not sentences: «Carla, 8», «Sevilla, flat», «1 brother, 1 cat», «pizza, dancing», «swim, draw».

The mind map helps you remember everything and put it in order. Consejo: los buenos escritores siempre planifican antes de escribir, ¡hasta en su lengua materna!

4. Sentences that start with I

Most sentences in your text start with I. Ojo: en inglés, I (yo) se escribe siempre con mayúscula, aunque esté en mitad de la frase: «My sister and I like music.»

Use the key verbs: I'm + name, age or adjective («I'm friendly»), I live in + place, I've got + family, pets, hair and eyes, I like / I love + things, I can + abilities. With these five you can write a lot!

5. Capital letters and full stops

Every sentence starts with a capital letter (mayúscula) and ends with a full stop (punto). «My name is Carla.» We also use capital letters for: names (Carla, Leo), places (Sevilla, Spain), days and months (Monday, May), languages and nationalities (English, Spanish) and I.

En castellano: en español «lunes», «mayo» y «español» van en minúscula. En inglés, no: Monday, May, Spanish llevan mayúscula.

6. Question marks, exclamation marks and commas

Besides full stops (.), we use other punctuation marks (signos de puntuación):

  • The question mark (?) goes at the end of a question: «What's your favourite food?»
  • The exclamation mark (!) shows surprise or strong feelings: «I love chocolate!» «Wow!»
  • The comma (,) separates things in a list: «I like apples, bananas and grapes.»

Very important! In English, question marks and exclamation marks go only at the end. We never write them at the beginning like in Spanish (¿…? ¡…!).

  • Spanish: «¿Tienes mascota?» English: «Have you got a pet?»

In a list, we don't usually put a comma before and: «red, blue and green».

Don't use too many exclamation marks! One is enough: «It's great!», not «It's great!!!!».

Activity: copy these sentences and add the punctuation: do you like pizza / I've got a cat a dog and a fish / what a beautiful day

7. Joining ideas: and, but, because

Short sentences are OK, but we can join them with connectors to make the text better. And (y) adds ideas: «I like dogs and cats.» But (pero) shows a contrast: «I can swim, but I can't dive.» Because (porque) gives a reason: «I love Saturdays because I play football.»

Compare: «I've got a cat. I've got a dog.» → «I've got a cat and a dog.» ¡Queda mucho mejor! Intenta usar cada conector al menos una vez.

8. Paragraphs

A good text has got paragraphs (párrafos): groups of sentences about the same idea. For a text about you, you can write three paragraphs. Paragraph 1: name, age, home and appearance. Paragraph 2: family and pets. Paragraph 3: likes, hobbies and abilities.

Start with a greeting, «Hello!» or «Hi!», and finish with a goodbye: «Write soon!» or «Bye for now!». Each paragraph starts on a new line.

9. Opening and closing sentences

A good text has got a beginning, a middle and an end.

The opening sentence (frase de inicio) says hello and tells the reader what the text is about:

  • «Hello! Let me tell you about me.»
  • «Hi! My name is Lucía and this is my story.»
  • «Do you want to know about me? Read on!»

In the middle, we write the information, in paragraphs: my family, my looks, my hobbies, my school.

The closing sentence (frase final) finishes the text in a nice way:

  • «That's all about me. Thanks for reading!»
  • «And what about you? What do you like?»
  • «I hope you like my text. Bye!»

A question at the end is a good idea: the reader wants to answer!

Each paragraph can also start with a topic sentence (frase principal) that tells the reader the topic: «Now let me tell you about my family.» «I've got lots of hobbies.»

Activity: write three different opening sentences and three closing sentences.

Vídeo: How to Write a Paragraph for Kids: Teaching Lesson in English · GRASPhopper (YouTube) · 789 mil visualizaciones

10. A model text

Read Carla's text: «Hello! My name's Carla and I'm eight years old. I live in a flat in Sevilla, in Spain. I've got long black hair and brown eyes.

I've got one brother, Leo, and a cat called Misi. My grandma lives with us. I love reading comics and dancing. My favourite food is pizza. I can swim very well, but I can't ride a horse. I love Saturdays because I go to the beach with my family. Write soon! Carla»

Vídeo: All About Me: English for kids · Primary World (YouTube) · 498 mil visualizaciones

11. An email to a pen pal

A pen pal (amigo por correspondencia) is a friend in another country. We write letters or emails to tell them about our life.

An email has got special parts:

  • Greeting (saludo): «Dear Jamie,» or «Hi Jamie,». Put a comma after the name.
  • Opening: «Thank you for your email.» «How are you?»
  • Body (cuerpo): the information in paragraphs: about me, my family, my hobbies, my town.
  • Questions for your pen pal: «Have you got a pet? What's your school like?»
  • Closing (despedida): «Write soon!» (¡Escríbeme pronto!) and «Best wishes,» or «Love,» (for family and close friends).
  • Your name.

Look: in an email to a friend we use contractions (formas cortas): I'm, I've got, don't, it's. It sounds friendly.

Tell your pen pal about things from your country: a typical food, a festival, a special place in your town.

Activity: write an email to Jamie from the reading. Answer his questions.

12. Check your writing

When you finish, read your text again and use a checklist: ✓ Have I got a greeting and a goodbye? ✓ Does every sentence start with a capital letter and end with a full stop? ✓ Is I always a capital letter? ✓ Have I used and, but and because? ✓ Have I written about my family, likes and abilities?

You can also swap texts with a partner and give two stars and a wish: two things you like and one thing to improve. «I like your connectors. I like your pet. Wish: use more capital letters.»

13. Make it interesting!

A good text has got details (detalles). Compare:

  • Boring: «I've got a dog. I like my dog.»
  • Interesting: «I've got a small brown dog called Rocky. He's really funny because he chases his tail!»

How can we make our writing interesting?

  • Add adjectives: big, small, beautiful, noisy, delicious, old, new.
  • Add names: «my friend Ana», «my town, Teruel».
  • Add reasons with because: «I love summer because I go to the beach.»
  • Add examples: «I like fruit, for example strawberries.»
  • Use really and very: «It's really exciting!»
  • Use different verbs: not only like, but love, enjoy, prefer.
  • Start sentences in different ways: not always «I…»: «On Saturdays, I…», «My favourite food is…».

Activity: make these sentences more interesting: «I've got a house. I like my school. I play a sport.»

14. Let's practise: my «All about me» poster

Now it's your turn! 1) Make your mind map. 2) Write your text in three paragraphs. 3) Check it with the checklist. 4) Copy it neatly onto a big card, with a photo or a self-portrait in the middle.

Hang the posters on the wall and do a gallery walk: walk around, read your classmates' posters and find something in common: «Lucas likes dogs too!», «Ana can swim, like me!». ¿Cuántas cosas en común encuentras?

15. My dreams for the future

We can finish our «All about me» text with our dreams (sueños) for the future.

To talk about jobs, we say When I grow up, I want to be… (Cuando sea mayor, quiero ser…):

  • «When I grow up, I want to be a vet because I love animals.»
  • «I want to be an astronaut because I want to travel to space.»
  • Other jobs: a teacher, a doctor, a nurse, a scientist, a firefighter (bombero), a footballer, a chef, a writer, an artist, a pilot.

Look: before a job we use a or an: a vet, an artist (an before a, e, i, o, u).

To talk about other dreams, we use I'd like to… (Me gustaría…):

  • «I'd like to visit Japan.»
  • «I'd like to learn to play the guitar.»
  • «I'd like to have a horse.»

Dreams can be big or small, and they can change. That's OK! The important thing is to work hard and enjoy learning.

Activity: write three sentences about your dreams with «I want to be…» and «I'd like to…».

Lo hacemos juntos

Une con and: «I like cats. I like dogs.»

  1. Las dos frases dicen lo mismo: me gusta.
  2. Une las cosas con and.

Resultado: I like cats and dogs.

Corrige: «my name is leo and i live in madrid»

  1. Mayúscula al empezar, en nombres, lugares e I.
  2. Punto al final.

Resultado: My name is Leo and I live in Madrid.

Da una razón con because: «I love summer…»

  1. Because da el porqué.
  2. Piensa algo que haces en verano.

Resultado: I love summer because I go to the beach.

Correct the punctuation: «¿Have you got a pet?»

  1. In English there is no ¿ at the beginning.
  2. The question mark goes only at the end.

Resultado: Have you got a pet?

Order: hair / I've got / brown / long

  1. Size goes before colour.
  2. Hair goes at the end.

Resultado: I've got long brown hair.

Errores típicos

  • Escribir i en minúscula: «i like» → «I like».
  • Olvidar la mayúscula en días e idiomas: «monday», «english» → «Monday», «English».
  • Escribir todo en una sola frase sin puntos.
  • Repetir siempre «I like…» sin conectores: une con and, but, because.
  • Empezar a escribir sin plan y olvidar partes importantes.
  • Writing ¿ and ¡ at the beginning of English sentences.
  • Saying «I want to be vet» without a or an.

PracticaResponde sin mirar arriba. Equivocarse aquí también enseña.

Ejercicios (24)

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

Nivel básico

  1. Escribe una frase con tu nombre y tu edad.

    Ver solución
    My name's… and I'm… years old.

  2. Escribe dónde vives.

    Ver solución
    I live in… (ciudad o pueblo).

  3. Describe tu pelo y tus ojos.

    Ver solución
    I've got short brown hair and green eyes (por ejemplo).

  4. How do you say «tímido» in English?

    Ver solución
    Shy.

  5. Where does Jamie live?

    Ver solución
    In Edinburgh, in Scotland.

  6. Which mark goes at the end of a question?

    Ver solución
    The question mark (?).

  7. Complete: «When I grow up, I want to be ___ artist.»

    Ver solución
    An.

  8. Write a greeting for an email.

    Ver solución
    Dear… / Hi…,

Nivel medio

  1. Pon mayúsculas: «on monday i speak english».

    Ver solución
    On Monday I speak English.

  2. Une con but: «I can draw. I can't sing.»

    Ver solución
    I can draw, but I can't sing.

  3. Completa con because: «I like Fridays ___ I go swimming.»

    Ver solución
    because.

  4. ¿Qué es un mind map?

    Ver solución
    Un mapa de ideas para planificar antes de escribir.

  5. Escribe un saludo y una despedida para tu texto.

    Ver solución
    Hello! … Write soon! (o Bye for now!).

  6. Describe Jamie's looks.

    Ver solución
    He's got short red hair and green eyes, he wears glasses and he's quite tall.

  7. Add commas: «I like red blue and green.»

    Ver solución
    I like red, blue and green.

  8. Write a closing sentence for your text.

    Ver solución
    Example: That's all about me. Thanks for reading!

  9. Translate: Me gustaría visitar Escocia.

    Ver solución
    I'd like to visit Scotland.

  10. What does Jamie want to be? Why?

    Ver solución
    A vet, because he loves animals.

Nivel avanzado

  1. Escribe dos cosas que comprobar al terminar.

    Ver solución
    Mayúsculas y puntos; usar and, but y because.

  2. Escribe un párrafo de 4 frases sobre ti.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: Hello! I'm Mario and I'm nine. I live in Zaragoza. I've got a sister and I love football because it's fun.

  3. Make this more interesting: «I've got a cat. I like it.»

    Ver solución
    Example: I've got a fluffy grey cat called Luna. I love her because she's very calm.

  4. Write an email to Jamie answering his questions.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  5. Write a paragraph about your personality with four adjectives.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  6. Write your full «All about me» text with an opening, three paragraphs and a closing.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

Explícalo con tus palabrasComo si se lo contaras a alguien de un curso menor

¿Has nombrado estas ideas?
★

Situación de aprendizajePen pals around the world

Each pupil writes an email to a pen pal in another country to introduce themselves, and the class makes a «Pen pals» display.

Pasos

  1. Plan the email with a mind map: me, family, hobbies, school, dreams.
  2. Write the email with a greeting, paragraphs, questions and a closing.
  3. Check capital letters, punctuation and details with a partner.
  4. Write the final version and put it on the display with a photo or drawing.

Producto final: An email to a pen pal and a class «Pen pals» display.

Cómo se valora

  • Describes looks and personality correctly.
  • Uses punctuation correctly, with ? and ! only at the end.
  • Organises the email with greeting, paragraphs and closing.
  • Adds details, reasons and questions for the reader.

Tarjetas de repasoToca la tarjeta para darle la vuelta

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • Leed en voz alta el texto «All about me» de vuestro hijo o hija y haced juntos la lista de comprobación.
  • Escribid entre todos un texto corto en inglés sobre la mascota o un familiar.
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Producción de textos escritos breves sobre uno mismo con planificación, conectores básicos (and, but, because), mayúsculas y puntuación, y autoevaluación (Lengua Extranjera: Inglés) (RD 157/2022, segundo ciclo de Primaria, 3.er curso).

  • Póster «All about me» y gallery walk.
  • Revisión entre iguales con «two stars and a wish».
  • Intercambio de cartas con otra clase o un colegio extranjero.

Fuentes y revisión

Revisado el 22 de noviembre de 2026.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Write a short text about yourself: name, age, family, likes and abilities
  • Use capital letters, full stops and the connectors and, but, because
  • Plan a text with a mind map before writing
  • Check and improve your writing with a checklist
  • Describe our looks and personality
  • Use question marks, exclamation marks and commas
  • Write opening and closing sentences
  • Write an email to a pen pal about ourselves

Palabras clave

about me · paragraph · capital letter · full stop · and · but · because · I'm · I've got · I like · I can · checklist

Tiempo

80 minutos hoy + 2 minutos en cada repaso
